title: Training Efficiency Evidence

supported_claims.statement: Trainable SVD reached the paired FP32 target in all 3 seeds for autonomous driving; the mean optimizer-step reduction was -23.33 ± 11.10%, below the predefined robust 10% criterion.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Three-seed validation completed, but the predefined robust >=10% efficiency rule was not satisfied.

supported_claims.statement: Trainable TT/MPS reached the paired FP32 target in 0/3 seeds for autonomous driving; therefore the experiment does not support a robust three-seed training-efficiency claim.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Target reach was incomplete across the three deterministic seeds.

supported_claims.statement: Trainable SVD reached the paired FP32 target in 0/3 seeds for robotics; therefore the experiment does not support a robust three-seed training-efficiency claim.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Target reach was incomplete across the three deterministic seeds.

supported_claims.statement: Trainable TT/MPS reached the paired FP32 target in 0/3 seeds for robotics; therefore the experiment does not support a robust three-seed training-efficiency claim.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Target reach was incomplete across the three deterministic seeds.

supported_claims.statement: Trainable SVD was architecturally reusable across both domains, but did not demonstrate robust training-efficiency improvement in both; target consistency was mixed and efficiency consistency was none.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Cross-domain comparison of the frozen three-seed experiments.

supported_claims.statement: Trainable TT/MPS was architecturally reusable across both domains, but did not demonstrate robust training-efficiency improvement in both; target consistency was weak and efficiency consistency was none.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Cross-domain comparison of the frozen three-seed experiments.

unsupported_claims.statement: Sprint 3 does not establish quantum advantage.
unsupported_claims.evidence_basis: TT/MPS is a quantum-inspired tensor-network method executed classically.

unsupported_claims.statement: Sprint 3 does not establish quantum speedup.
unsupported_claims.evidence_basis: No quantum hardware or quantum runtime comparison was performed.

unsupported_claims.statement: Sprint 3 does not establish native TT/MPS runtime acceleration.
unsupported_claims.evidence_basis: The current TT/MPS forward path reconstructs a temporary differentiable dense-equivalent weight during classical execution.

unsupported_claims.statement: Sprint 3 does not establish performance on full-scale production 7B-class VLA models.
unsupported_claims.evidence_basis: The pilot uses compact synthetic driving and robotics proxy tasks.

matched_ablation.interpretation: Neither matched representation reached the paired FP32 target.
Neither matched representation reached the paired FP32 target.

quantum_inspired_method: Trainable Tensor Train / open-boundary Matrix Product State parameterization (TT/MPS), executed classically.
limitations: Experiments use compact synthetic autonomous-driving and robotics proxy tasks.
The pilot does not train or evaluate a full 7B-class production VLA model.
The lightweight language component is a trainable hashed-token embedding encoder, not a large Transformer language model.
CPU wall-clock timing is descriptive; optimizer steps and samples to target are the primary efficiency measures.
TT/MPS executes classically and does not constitute a quantum-hardware speedup.
The matched SVD-vs-TT/MPS ablation uses seed 42 as a controlled isolation experiment.
Architectural reuse across domains does not imply one universally trained model.
